details.title: About downgrading Revit {from} to Revit {to}
details.why: Revit {to} cannot open a file saved in Revit {from}: a Revit release only opens files from its own version and older ones. Revit Downgrade rewrites the file in the Revit {to} format, so it opens in Revit {to} as a normal, editable Revit file, with no IFC or other export in between.
details.steps: This is a one-version step, {route}. Anything Revit {to} does not know is removed, and every removed element is listed on the result page. | The file goes down {n} versions, one at a time: {route}. Each step removes what the version below does not know, and every removed element is listed on the result page.
details.time: Small files take about a minute; large models take a few minutes. | Small files take a minute or two; large models take a few minutes for each of the {n} versions.
details.opensIn: The converted file opens in Revit {to} and in any newer Revit, which upgrades it as usual. Save it once in Revit {to} and it is an ordinary Revit {to} file from then on.
details.files: It works the same for projects (.rvt), project templates (.rte), families (.rfa) and family templates (.rft) saved in Revit {from}, up to 1 GB.

alternatives.title: Other ways to get a Revit {from} model into Revit {to}
alternatives.intro: Converting is not the only option. What each one gives the person on Revit {to}:

items.label: A copy from before the upgrade
items.text: If the sender still has the file saved in Revit {to} or older, it opens as it is, but without the changes made since.

items.label: IFC
items.text: Revit {from} exports IFC and Revit {to} links or imports it. Geometry and much of the data arrive, but walls, families and parameters are no longer native, editable Revit elements.

items.label: Installing Revit {from}
items.text: Opens the file as it is, but needs a Revit {from} license, and anything saved there can no longer be opened by people who stay on Revit {to}.

items.label: Converting the file
items.text: A native Revit {to} file you keep working on. Elements Revit {to} has no place for are removed and listed with their ElementIds.

changes.title: What Revit {to} does not support
changes.intro: Each Revit release adds new kinds of elements. When a file goes down, elements the older version has no place for are removed, and every one of them is listed on the result page with its ElementId, so you can find it in the original model.

2027.removed: point, line and area boundary conditions in the new Revit 2027 categories, rebar distribution paths and rebar concrete edges.
2027.other: the "Server Room" space type becomes no space type, and stair riser numbers go back to the size and color settings of Revit 2026.

2026.removed: rebar crank types and MEP system zone color fills.
2026.other: toposolid sub-divisions are kept as toposolids; a toposolid shaped from a mesh keeps its solid but loses the mesh shape; cable types and conductor sizes become Revit 2025 wire types and sizes.

2025.removed: sheet collections, pipe and duct analytical segments, rebar splice types and splice lines.
2025.other: "Apparent power" labels go back to the older "load" wording.

2024.removed: electrical connectors, electrical load cases, rebar bending details, and wall and floor layer elements.

2023.removed: plumbing equipment, mechanical control devices, MEP ancillary framing, fabrication ductwork stiffeners, electrical load sets, analytical feeders and transformers, analytical panels and openings, and tags of categories that can only be tagged from Revit 2023 (such as column, model group and link tags).

howTo.q: How do I downgrade a Revit file to an older version?
howTo.a: Add your file above, choose the Revit version you need and press Downgrade, then download the converted file and open it in that older Revit. For example, a Revit 2026 model can be opened in Revit 2024. Any file from Revit 2023 to 2027 can go down to Revit 2022, with nothing to install.

saveOlder.q: Can Revit save a file to an older version?
saveOlder.a: No. Revit only upgrades: it opens files from older versions and always saves in its own version. There is no "Save As older version" in Revit, which is why this tool exists.

supported.q: Which files and versions are supported?
supported.a: Projects (.rvt), project templates (.rte), families (.rfa) and family templates (.rft) saved in Revit 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 or 2027, converted to any older version down to Revit 2022. Files up to 1 GB.

lost.a: Elements that the older Revit does not know, such as features added in a newer version, are removed. After the conversion you see the full list of removed elements with their ElementIds and can download it as CSV.

backsave.q: Can I backsave a Revit file?
backsave.a: Not in Revit itself: Revit has no backsave or "save to previous version" command. Revit Downgrade does the backsave online instead, for files from Revit 2023 to 2027, down to Revit 2022.

safe.a: Your original file is deleted as soon as the conversion finishes, and the converted file after 2 hours. Files are never shared. If a conversion fails, the file is kept for up to 7 days to fix the problem, without you ticking anything, and you can delete it at once with Delete my file. After that the server keeps only the error message, not the file. The website and server code that handles files is open source; the conversion engine itself is closed source.

workshared.q: Can I downgrade a workshared (central) model?
workshared.a: Yes. Worksets and worksharing are kept. Convert the central model like any other file. A cloud model in Autodesk Docs has to be saved as a local .rvt file first.

links.q: What about families and linked models?
links.a: Families loaded in a model are converted with it, so there is nothing extra to do. A linked Revit model is a separate file, so convert it on its own, to the same version. The same goes for a family file (.rfa) you want to load later.

howTo.q: How do I open a Revit {from} file in Revit {to}?
howTo.a: Add the file above: Revit {to} is picked for you. Press Downgrade, then download the converted file and open it in Revit {to}. Nothing to install, no account.

saveOlder.q: Can Revit {from} save a file for Revit {to}?
saveOlder.a: No. Revit {from} has no Save As older version: every save writes the Revit {from} format, which Revit {to} cannot open. Converting the file is the way to get it into Revit {to}.
